findings.description: The instance user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in plain text. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and from the instance metadata service, so these long-lived credentials are effectively disclosed.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", so the legacy unauthenticated instance metadata service (IMDSv1) remains enabled. An SSRF in the web application can then retrieve instance credentials.
No root_block_device / ebs_block_device configuration with encrypted = true, so the instance's attached storage is created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

findings.issue_category: instance in public subnet with public IP
findings.description: The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and is directly reachable from the internet (public_dns is exported), placing compute that could sit behind a load balancer directly on the internet edge.

The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is deliberately commented out), so block storage attached to the web host stores data unencrypted and any snapshot of it is also unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and therefore is itself unencrypted; snapshots are easily shared/copied across accounts, exposing the data if permissions are ever loosened.
Ingress allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet for brute-force and exploitation attempts.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no HTTPS/TLS listener configured, so all traffic to end users travels in cleartext and is subject to interception or tampering.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched in this subnet receives a public IP address, removing the private network layer for components that do not need inbound internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically exposes all instances in this subnet to the internet with public addressing rather than keeping them in a private layer.
The bucket that receives VPC flow logs has no server_side_encryption_configuration and no KMS customer-managed key, so sensitive network audit data is stored without enforced encryption.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy restricting access is configured for the flow log bucket, so account-level or accidental permissive policies could expose network telemetry publicly.
force_destroy = true with no versioning, MFA delete, or object lock allows the VPC flow log audit trail to be deleted wholesale, destroying forensic evidence.
